goals.text:
【研究命题·纯机器学习/数学】

解空间刚性 = 满足全部解析约束的函数集合的维数：低维/唯一 = 刚，高维/连续族 = 胖。

核心问题：小型前馈网络的“泛化行为”能否作为 bootstrap 解空间刚性的探针？
令 w = 约束样本数，N_c(w) = 在未参与训练的留出约束点上取得“零违规”所需的最小网络容量（用隐藏层宽度度量）。

【唯一硬性口径（不可更改，其余全由你决定）】
- 零违规 = 留出约束点上的最大绝对误差 ≤ 1e-3。
- 刚性 = 扫描范围内存在较小的有限 N_c（且 N_c 不随 w 增长）；胖 = 扫描上限内任何宽度都达不到零违规（N_c 不可达）。判别是二值的。
- 所有报告数值必须是有限数（禁止 inf/nan/None）。
- 研究对象只能是小型前馈网络本身。严禁把本命题替换或“换名归约”为材料/化学/玻璃/合金/离子导电等任何物理体系，也不要用别的领域类比回答。

【实验的族、样本、扫描、脚本如何设计，以及如何证明“刚性可达”，由你自己决定并给出理由。】

所有结论必须来自真实运行的可复现数值实验：给出扫描设置、训练与留出误差数值、以及 N_c(w) 的数值与趋势。

unknowns.text: The core proposition assumes that generalization performance (zero violation on held-out constraints) directly proxies solution space rigidity, but this may conflate empirical fit with geometric structure — a network might generalize well due to implicit regularization or overparameterization bias rather than because the true solution set is low-dimensional.

“Zero violation” defined as max absolute error ≤ 1e-3 is numerically fragile; floating-point precision limits, optimizer convergence tolerance, and gradient clipping may prevent reaching this threshold even when analytically possible, leading to false “fat” classification.

No ground-truth solution space dimension is provided for validation — without knowing whether the underlying constraint system is truly rigid or胖 in theory, N_c(w) trends cannot be validated against truth, making the probe uncalibrated.

The assumption that hidden width N_c adequately captures model capacity ignores depth, activation function nonlinearity, and initialization effects — a narrow deep network may fit better than a wide shallow one despite same parameter count, confounding N_c interpretation.

For small w (few constraints), even minimal-width networks may trivially interpolate training points and coincidentally satisfy held-out constraints by chance, falsely suggesting rigidity; conversely, large w may saturate any finite-width network regardless of true solution space geometry.

Defining "zero violation" solely by max absolute error ≤ 1e-3 may overlook structural mismatches in function class approximation (e.g., oscillatory vs. smooth targets), leading to false rigidity claims even when N_c is sufficient.

Gradient-based optimization may converge to local minima that satisfy training constraints but fail on out-of-sample points, causing N_c(w) to be overestimated or mischaracterized as “fat” when it’s actually rigid.
No ground-truth analytical solution or benchmark dataset is specified; without known reference functions, validation of “zero violation” and N_c(w) trends lacks objective calibration.
As w increases, the constraint set may become ill-conditioned or numerically unstable, especially if constraints are linearly dependent or nearly so, making N_c(w) artificially high or erratic.

The assumption that hidden layer width alone captures network capacity ignores depth, activation function choice, and initialization — all of which can dramatically affect representational power and generalization behavior.
I don’t understand why the simulation produced only repeated “4” values instead of computed results — is this a default initialization bug, or an intentional fallback?
I never considered that the test runner might skip execution entirely if certain preconditions aren’t met silently, without throwing an error or warning.
